headline: Enterprise patch pressure mounted as SAP shipped critical fixes while researchers exposed unpatched flaws in AI coding tools that read inboxes and run attacker code.

emerging_trends.text: Unpatched flaws in AI developer tools keep stacking up, with Cursor still auto-running malicious code from poisoned repositories and Claude for Chrome exposing Gmail and Calendar to rival extensions long after disclosure.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Unpatched Flaws in Claude for Chrome and Cursor

emerging_trends.text: Enterprise software shipped a heavy patch load, led by SAP fixes for critical NetWeaver, AppRouter, and Commerce Cloud holes that expose corporate data and knock systems offline.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SAP Patches Critical NetWeaver, AppRouter, and Commerce Cloud Flaws

emerging_trends.text: The fight over Microsoft 365 sign-ins intensified as the new Jalisco and OmegaLord kits punched straight through multi-factor authentication.
emerging_trends.topic_title: New Phishing Kits Defeat Microsoft 365 MFA

topics.title: SAP Patches Critical NetWeaver, AppRouter, and Commerce Cloud Flaws
topics.latest_developments: SAP's July 2026 security updates fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including three critical flaws in NetWeaver, Commerce Cloud, and the AppRouter that let attackers read and alter data, knock systems offline, and desynchronize request-response traffic.
topics.summary: SAP runs the core finance, supply-chain, and commerce systems at most large enterprises. Administrators should apply the July notes promptly because the critical bugs threaten both data integrity and availability.

sources.title: SAP warns of critical flaws in NetWeaver and Commerce Cloud
SAP Patches Critical Vulnerabilities in NetWeaver, Approuter, Commerce Cloud

topics.title: Unpatched Flaws in Claude for Chrome and Cursor
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported that a ClaudeBleed-linked flaw in Claude for Chrome survives eight patches and lets other browser extensions read a user's Gmail and Calendar, while Dark Reading found Cursor still auto-runs malicious code hidden in poisoned repositories seven months after researchers alerted the company in December.
topics.summary: AI coding assistants and browser agents hold broad access to code, inboxes, and calendars, and these unpatched flaws let a poisoned repository or rogue extension turn that access against the user. Treat untrusted repositories and extensions as hostile until the vendors ship fixes.

sources.title: Unpatched Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Extensions Read Gmail, Calendar
Cursor IDE Auto-Executes Malicious Code in Poisoned Repos

topics.title: New Phishing Kits Defeat Microsoft 365 MFA
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed two new phishing kits, Jalisco and OmegaLord, that target Microsoft 365 accounts and defeat multi-factor authentication, alongside the Forg365 service that chains device-code phishing and adversary-in-the-middle session theft.
topics.summary: The kits intercept session tokens to walk past MFA and seize Microsoft 365 mailboxes for extortion. Enforcing phishing-resistant passkeys and tight conditional-access policies blunts them.

sources.title: New phishing kits target Microsoft 365 accounts, evade MFA
Forg365 PhaaS Targets Microsoft 365 with Device Code and AitM Session Theft

topics.title: Old Signed Shims Bypass UEFI Secure Boot
topics.latest_developments: ESET disclosed that eleven Microsoft-signed shims at version 0.9 or below undo Secure Boot on nearly every UEFI PC that trusts them, and Microsoft revoked the vulnerable loaders in its June update.
topics.summary: A shim is a small first-stage loader Microsoft signs so Linux and boot tools run with Secure Boot on, and the outdated versions let an attacker bypass the protection outright. Apply the June revocations and inventory boot media for the old shims.

sources.title: No one knows how many old shims can still bypass UEFI Secure Boot

topics.title: Pentagon Suspends CMMC Phase 2
topics.latest_developments: The Pentagon suspended Phase 2 of its Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification program and stood up a review-and-reform task force to reexamine the contractor security rules.
topics.summary: CMMC sets cybersecurity requirements across the U.S. defense industrial base, and the pause delays enforcement while the task force conducts a comprehensive review. Contractors gain more time before certification requirements take hold.

sources.title: Pentagon Suspends CMMC Phase 2 as It Rethinks Contractor Cybersecurity Rules

topics.title: GigaWiper Modular Backdoor and Wiper
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading profiled GigaWiper, a modular implant that borrows code from several malware families to combine backdoor access with destructive wiping, letting each operator choose the damage it inflicts.
topics.summary: GigaWiper hands attackers persistent control and a data-destruction payload in one tool, maximizing impact while keeping their own footprint small. Its modular design lets operators tune the destructive stage per target.

sources.title: GigaWiper Lets Threat Actors Choose Their Own Destructive Attack

business_politics.title: U.S. Inflation Slows to 3.5% in June
business_politics.latest_developments: June consumer prices rose 3.5% year over year, a sharper cooldown than economists forecast, as tumbling gasoline prices offset the U.S.-Iran oil shock and traders pared bets on Federal Reserve rate rises.
business_politics.summary: The U.S. consumer-price index climbed 3.5% in the year through June, easing more than expected as falling petrol prices countered the energy spike from the war with Iran; the softer reading tempered fears that Middle East fighting would reignite inflation and force the Federal Reserve to tighten.

sources.title: US inflation fell more than expected to 3.5% in June as petrol prices tumbled
Stock Market Today: Big Banks' Bumper Quarter Points to Strong U.S. Economy

business_politics.title: Wall Street Banks Post Blockbuster Quarter
business_politics.latest_developments: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Bank of America opened earnings season Tuesday with bumper profits driven by an equities-trading boom, signaling a resilient U.S. economy despite the oil-war backdrop.
business_politics.summary: The largest U.S. banks reported strong quarterly results as booming equities trading lifted profits, a sign of underlying economic strength as the Federal Reserve weighs its rate path during the Iran conflict.

sources.title: Wall Street banks post blockbuster profits as equities trading booms

business.title: Falling Gas Prices Ease Local Inflation
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported June's national inflation cooled to 3.5% as pump prices fell, while warning the renewed Iran war could stall further relief for Pittsburgh-area households.
business.summary: Lower gasoline prices cut inflation for western Pennsylvania consumers in June, though the Post-Gazette cautioned that the renewed U.S.-Iran war and climbing oil prices could limit further progress at the pump.

sources.title: Falling gas prices cut inflation last month, yet renewal of Iran war could limit progress

business.title: Next Generation of Pittsburgh Restaurateurs
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled a rising class of Pittsburgh restaurateurs, among them John Paradise and Itai Tuti, building the region's dining scene.
business.summary: Younger Pittsburgh chefs and owners, including John Paradise and Itai Tuti, are opening and running restaurants across the region, pursuing food as a calling in a Post-Gazette feature on the city's dining future.

sources.title: 'The next generation' of Pittsburgh restaurateurs pursue their passion for food

around_town.title: Another 90-Degree Stretch and Storm Risk
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA forecasts highs in the 90s Tuesday through Friday—all First Alert Weather Days—with a severe-storm setup possible Saturday, as an air-quality alert covers western Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: The Pittsburgh region faces four straight days of 90-degree heat from Tuesday, July 14, through Friday, with higher heat-index values and a Pennsylvania DEP air-quality alert; forecasters flag Saturday for possible severe storms and the city keeps cooling centers open.

sources.title: Another stretch of high temperatures in the 90s hitting the Pittsburgh area this week
Morning Roundup: Air quality alert issued for Western Pa.; Pittsburgh opens cooling centers amid heat wave

around_town.title: Dozens of Cats Rescued in Perry North
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's Bureau of Animal Care and Control and local rescues removed at least 60 cats from a Franklin Road home in Perry North that one volunteer said smelled of 'ammonia and death.'
around_town.summary: An ongoing operation pulled dozens of cats—officials estimate at least 60—from a home on Franklin Road in Pittsburgh's Perry North neighborhood, with the Bureau of Animal Care and Control and volunteers including Anna Montano working the scene.

sources.title: At least 30 cats rescued from Pittsburgh home that smelled like "ammonia and death"

around_town.title: Frick Park Trackchair Program Widens Access
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine spotlighted Frick Park's all-terrain Trackchair program, which lets visitors with limited mobility, including teens Hailey Tucker and Maddock Wall, roll the park's trails together.
around_town.summary: Frick Park's Trackchair program offers all-terrain power wheelchairs so people with limited mobility can navigate the park's trails; Pittsburgh Magazine profiled Hailey Tucker and Maddock 'Doc' Wall exploring the outdoors with them.

sources.title: Frick Park's Trackchair Program Allows Lovebirds to Explore the Great Outdoors Together

events.title: Bloop Vintage-Tech Museum in Penn Hills
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette featured Bloop, a grassroots museum of vintage technology taking shape in Penn Hills.
events.summary: Bloop, a grassroots museum in Penn Hills, gathers vintage computers and gadgets for enthusiasts to browse, an emerging spot for fans of old technology in the eastern suburbs.

sources.title: In Penn Hills, Bloop showcases burgeoning grassroots museum of vintage technology

events.title: Tours at the Carnegie Carnegie
events.latest_developments: NEXTpittsburgh toured the Andrew Carnegie Free Library & Music Hall in Carnegie, spotlighting its music hall, secret passages, and ghost lore.
events.summary: The Andrew Carnegie Free Library & Music Hall—the 'Carnegie Carnegie' in Carnegie, Pennsylvania—opens its historic music hall and reputedly haunted passages to visitors, guided by executive director Marlee Gallagher and library staff.

sources.title: Ghosts and secret passages at the Carnegie Carnegie

around_teams.title: Braxton Ashcraft's Road to the All-Star Game
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette traced Pirates right-hander Braxton Ashcraft's path from a high-school football star through a run of major injuries to his first All-Star selection.
around_teams.summary: Pirates pitcher Braxton Ashcraft, a onetime gridiron standout who battled serious injuries in the minors, reached the 2026 All-Star Game in Philadelphia as a National League replacement, and the Post-Gazette chronicled the journey.

sources.title: 'The kid had a vision': Inside Braxton Ashcraft's journey from gridiron stardom through injuries to his All-Star debut

team_usa.title: MLB's 2028 Olympic Bid Hits Union Snags
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported growing support to send major-leaguers to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics runs into disputes with the players' union over tickets and accommodations.
team_usa.summary: Momentum is building to put big-league players in the 2028 Los Angeles Games, but ESPN sources say disagreements between Major League Baseball and the MLB Players Association over matters like tickets and hotel rooms complicate baseball's Olympic return on home soil.

sources.title: Sources: MLB in LA28 facing hurdles with MLBPA

team_usa.title: Rethinking the USMNT's World Cup Failure
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN argued the U.S. men's World Cup shortcomings resist a fix through overhauling youth development, suggesting the program is progressing and luck ran against it.
team_usa.summary: Days after the U.S. men's national team's round-of-16 exit from the home World Cup, ESPN pushed back on calls to remake American youth soccer, contending the United States keeps making progress and simply lacked luck.

sources.title: The USMNT's struggles at the World Cup can't be fixed by overhauling youth development
